chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the sacrificial animal whose ear is torn, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'If its tear is a mark (from branding), then there is no problem, and if it is a tear, then it is not suitable.'

key_terms.الضَّحِيَّةِ: Sacrificial animal offered during Eid al-Adha
key_terms.شَقًّا: A tear or split (natural or physical injury)
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / it is permissible
key_terms.فَلَا يَصْلُحُ: It is not suitable / not valid
key_terms.وَسْمًا: A mark or brand (typically from cattle)

ai.seo_question: Is a sacrificial animal with a torn ear valid for Qurbani?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between a branding mark (wasm), which is an external addition and thus permissible, and a natural tear (shaq), which is a structural defect rendering the animal unsuitable. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that minor, non-inherent imperfections do not invalidate the sacrifice, while inherent physical flaws do. The distinction highlights the importance of the animal's natural integrity in fulfilling the religious obligation of Udhiyah.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the slaughter which happens to have torn ears. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If its tear is a mark, so there is no problem, and if it was a tear, so it is not correct’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of an offering with torn ears. He (the Imam) said, ‘If the tear is a mark it is not harmful; but if it is a rip then it is not acceptable.’”
